nodes.characterization_summary: Co3O4 shows band gap of 1.2 eV; Co3-xO4 with Co cation defects exhibits increased DOS near Fermi level and reduced band gap.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the sample of perfect Co3O4 has a band gap of 1.2 eV, as shown in the DOS results in Figure 2a.[63] However, after inducing the Co cation defects to form Co3-xO4, we can clearly see that an increased DOS formed above the Fermi level, leading to a much smaller energy gap

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine MnO2 has band gap of 1.55 eV indicating semiconductor properties; Mn cation vacancy defects create continuous DOS around Fermi level yielding half-metallic properties.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pristine MnO2 shows a band gap of 1.55 eV, indicating the property of semiconductors. In contrast, it will form a continuous DOS around the Fermi level after inducing Mn cation vacancy defects and show half-metallic properties

nodes.characterization_summary: CoSe2 with Fe doping and Co vacancy has charge transfer resistance of 4.2 Ω (smallest among variants: pure CoSe2 10.5 Ω, Fe-doped 5.3 Ω, Fe-doped+Se vacancy 5.4 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the CoSe2 with Fe doping and Co vacancy shows smallest charge transfer resistances (4.2 Ω) which is much lower than that of pure CoSe2 (10.5 Ω), CoSe2 with Fe doping (5.3 Ω), and CoSe2 with Fe doping and Se vacancy (5.4 Ω)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni2P with Ni vacancy defects shows lower charge transfer resistance than Ni2P or Mn doped Ni2P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the EIS result shown in Figure 2e, Ni2P with Ni vacancy defects shows lower charge transfer resistance than that of Ni2P or even Mn doped Ni2P...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM directly visualizes Co cation vacancies in Co3O4 as lower intensity regions marked by red circles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By this technology, the imaging contrast intensity is proportional to the atomic number, so the bright points shown in Figure 11a should be the Co atoms... We can see that many Co cation vacancies exist in Figure 11a, which are marked by red circles.

nodes.characterization_summary: α-Ni(OH)2 samples with increasing Ni vacancies show gradually decreased Ni-Ni coordination peak intensity at ≈2.68 Å in FT-EXAFS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak at ≈2.68 Å represents the Ni-Ni bond; the intensity is related to their coordination environment. Therefore, we can obtain the coordination number from the results and identify the situation of defects. The intensity of the Ni-Ni bond decreased gradually from sample 1 to sample 4, indicating that more Ni vacancies formed.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH with cation vacancies shows Ia/Ib ratio (528/457 cm⁻¹) increasing from lower potential (1.024 V) than pristine NiFe LDH (1.224 V), indicating enhanced defective Ni(OH)x formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the value of Ia/Ib for NiFe LDH with metal vacancies started to increase at 1.024 V, which is much lower than that of NiFe LDH (1.224 V). What's more, the larger change in the value from the beginning to the maximum at 1.424 V for NiFe LDH with metal vacancies indicated that it underwent more obvious restructuring

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-doped NiO with metal vacancies shows Ni K-edge main peak intensity decreasing with increasing potential (indicating Ni²⁺→Ni²⁺ᵟ oxidation), unlike stable pure NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the main peak of Fe-doped NiO with metal vacancies decreased gradually with increasing potential. However, for pure NiO, the intensity of the Ni K-edge main peak remained nearly unchanged. The decreased intensity of the main peak is due to the oxidation of Ni²⁺ to Ni²⁺ᵟ with increasing potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNi2O4 with Fe vacancies shows reduced intensities of Fe-O, Fe-Fe, Fe-Ni coordination peaks in FT-EXAFS while Ni-based coordination peaks remain stable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further comparing the Fourier transformation from the EXAFS spectra shown in Figure 12j–k shows that the intensities of Fe-based bonds, including Fe-O, Fe-Fe, and Fe-Ni, become slightly lower, while those of Ni-based bonds (Ni-O, Ni-Ni, and Ni-Fe) do not show obvious
